sections.h2: Gold is 89% of India's Swiss imports, and TEPA does not change its duty

chart.title: Gold, pearls and precious stones dominate India's imports from Switzerland
chart.sub: India's imports from Switzerland, 2024, US$ billion.
chart.source: Secondary compilations of Swiss customs and DGCI&S data, as reported in the post.

sections.means: Gold's effective duty does not change under TEPA, so the headline import figure is mostly not a TEPA exposure.
sections.todo: Strip gold out of gross trade figures before measuring what TEPA exposes India to.

sections.means: Basmati and non-basmati rice get duty-free EFTA access with no reciprocal concession from India.
sections.todo: Actively market the duty-free rice access to exporters, as the post recommends.

sections.h2: Norway sells India about 200 tonnes of salmon, against 52,000 to China

chart.title: TEPA removes the tariff, but India's salmon market still has to be built
chart.sub: Norwegian salmon sales this year, tonnes.
chart.source: Norwegian Seafood Council, as reported in the post.

sections.means: Norway sold roughly 52,000 tonnes of salmon to China this year, against about 200 tonnes to India.
sections.todo: Pair the tariff cut with cold-chain and distribution investment before expecting salmon volumes to follow.
